# `binding_store.py` is at 787/800 — extract the last-synced-peer-state cluster

Raised by the operator while reviewing change 1296 (ticket 88d9): "We're adding a lot to
binding_store.py. Should we split that out to preemptively avoid the 800 LOC cap?" Measured rather
than estimated: the file was **749** LOC, 1296 takes it to **787**, and the cap is **800**. Thirteen
lines of headroom, and the CI module-size gate fails the build when ANY `src/rebar` file exceeds the
cap — so the next contributor to touch this file breaks the build, having added nothing wrong.

Deliberately NOT done inside 1296: that change is a data-loss fix that needed to land promptly, and
bundling a structural refactor into it would have made it slower to review and harder to reason about.
The docstrings added there were tightened instead (795 -> 787) to buy immediate headroom.

## The seam, which already exists

`binding_store.py` holds two distinct concerns:

1. **binding lifecycle** — bind / confirm / unbind, absence + rekey handling, GC/retire grace, the
   immutable numeric Jira id (bug 7c26). This is the bulk of the file.
2. **last-synced PEER STATE** — the ADR-0026 three-way-merge baseline (`get_baseline`, `set_baseline`,
   `seed_baselines_from_snapshot`, `_BASELINE_FIELDS`) plus the peer-parent evidence channel added by
   1296 (`get_peer_parent`, `set_peer_parent`). Together ~130 LOC with docstrings — comfortably over
   the policy's 100-LOC floor for a new module, and a genuine cohesive concern: "what did the peer
   look like the last time we successfully looked".

Concern 2 has its own ADR, its own absence semantics ("an ABSENT baseline is VALID and degrades to
local-wins"), and its own advance site in the pass (`reconcile._advance_baselines` /
`_advance_peer_parent`). Its consumers are `outbound_field_diff`, `binding_walk` and now
`inbound_fields` — none of which touch binding lifecycle.

## What makes this non-trivial, stated honestly

These are METHODS on `BindingStore`, not free functions, so this is not a file move. Extraction means
either module-level helpers taking the entry dict (the store keeps thin delegating methods, so no
caller changes) or a mixin. The first is preferable — it keeps the public surface identical, so every
existing call site and every test double stays valid, and it makes the peer-state functions directly
unit-testable without constructing a store.

Per the module-size policy this must be split ALONG THE SEAM ABOVE and not mechanically to hit a
number, and the new module must not fall under 100 LOC.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `binding_store.py` is under 700 LOC, and the new module is over 100
- [x] `BindingStore`'s public surface is UNCHANGED — no call site and no test double is edited to
      accommodate the split, asserted by the fact that the reconciler suites pass untouched
- [x] the peer-state functions are directly unit-testable without constructing a `BindingStore`, and
      at least one new test does so (otherwise the extraction bought nothing)
- [x] `_BASELINE_FIELDS` moves WITH the cluster, and `outbound_field_diff` / `binding_walk` /
      `inbound_fields` still resolve their reads (a grep-backed consumer list recorded on this ticket)
- [x] the absence semantics survive the move verbatim: absent baseline degrades to local-wins, absent
      peer parent degrades to NO CLEAR. A test pins each, because these are the properties that make
      the cluster safe and a refactor is exactly when they get quietly dropped
- [x] the module-size gate passes, and the full reconciler unit + integration suites pass
